short: one keyword-led part of a statement, like FROM products or WHERE NOT discontinued. in a SELECT, each takes a table and hands one on.
a name SELECT gives an output column with AS. it exists from SELECT on, so ORDER BY can use it and WHERE can't.
a column of the result, named by SELECT. ORDER BY and GROUP BY may refer to one by name or position, WHERE and HAVING never.
a column of the table FROM built. a name inside an expression is always looked up here, even in ORDER BY.
anything that computes a value from a row: a column, a literal, a function call, price * 1.2. SELECT runs its list once per row.
an expression that answers true, false or unknown, like price > 50. WHERE keeps the rows where it's true.
which operator binds first when there are no parentheses: NOT, then AND, then OR.
SQL's logic with a third truth value, unknown, for comparisons involving NULL.
the truth value of a comparison with NULL. WHERE drops it like false; CHECK lets it pass. postgres stores it as a NULL boolean.
a comparison that treats NULL as a value: two NULLs are not distinct, NULL and 5 are. it never answers unknown.
a sort option that puts NULLs before every value. postgres's default is NULLS LAST going up and NULLS FIRST going down.
an ORDER BY whose keys tell every row apart, usually by ending with a unique key, so ties can't shuffle.
the standard spelling of LIMIT: FETCH FIRST 10 ROWS ONLY. postgres accepts both.
a FETCH FIRST option that keeps going past n rows while they tie with the last one on the ORDER BY keys.
skips the first n rows of a result. it reads every row it skips, so deep pages get slower.
removes duplicate output rows, comparing whole rows after SELECT. two NULLs count as duplicates.
postgres only: keeps the first row for each value of its keys, first by the ORDER BY, which must start with them.
if/else as an expression: the first WHEN that's true gives the value, otherwise the ELSE, otherwise NULL.
returns its first argument that isn't NULL. an empty string or a 0 counts as a value.
NULLIF(a, b) returns NULL when a equals b, and a otherwise. the divide-by-zero guard: x / NULLIF(y, 0).
matches text against a pattern: % is any run of characters, _ is exactly one. case-sensitive; ILIKE isn't.
a pattern language for text. postgres matches POSIX regexes with ~, and ignores case with ~*.
comparing text by its bytes: capitals before small letters, accented letters after both. what the browser engine uses.
folds many rows into one value: count, sum, avg, min, max. every one but count(*) skips NULLs.
sorts rows into buckets, one per different key, and hands on one row per bucket.
filters buckets after GROUP BY, so it can use aggregates. a condition on single rows belongs in WHERE.
